core_obligations: Take nonzero a and b in R and apply the elementary divisor property to the 1 by 2 matrix (a b) to obtain an invertible u and an invertible matrix V with u(a b)V = (f 0) (proof lines 37824-37826).
Read off f = u a g_11 + u b g_21 and, from invertibility of V, that g_11 and g_21 generate the unit ideal (proof lines 37826-37828).

Conclude that the ideal generated by a and b equals the principal ideal generated by f, and obtain the general case by the induction on the number of generators that the author states without details (proof lines 37828-37830).

difficulty_reason: The lemma relates two notions for domains: an elementary divisor domain, in which every matrix can be put in Smith normal form by row and column operations over the ring, is a Bezout domain, meaning every finitely generated ideal is principal (statement lines 37819-37821). The proof is an 8-line argument (proof lines 37824-37831) that applies the defining property of an elementary divisor domain to the 1 by 2 matrix (a b): one takes invertible u in R and an invertible 2 by 2 matrix V with u(a b)V = (f 0), reads off that f lies in the ideal (a, b) while a and b are combinations of f with coefficients from the first column of V^-1, and uses the invertibility of V to see that the entries g_11 and g_21 generate the unit ideal. The author closes with an induction on the number of generators whose details are omitted. The content is therefore the two-element case, which is carried out completely; the passage to an arbitrary finite set of generators is the part the author leaves out.
